import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1176

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1176](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1176)
-/

open Cardinal

namespace Erdos1176

/--
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

A problem of Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal. The consistency of this was proved by Hajnal and Komjáth.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_1176 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = aleph 1 →
      ∃ (EColor : Type) (_ : mk EColor = aleph 1) (c_edge : G.edgeSet → EColor),
        ∀ (VColor : Type) (_ : mk VColor ≤ aleph 0) (c_vert : V → VColor),
          ∃ (vc : VColor),
            ∀ (ec : EColor), ∃ (u v : V) (h : G.Adj u v),
              c_vert u = vc ∧ c_vert v = vc ∧ c_edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩ = ec := by
  sorry

end Erdos1176

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses universe-0 colour palettes, existentially choosing an edge palette of cardinality ℵ₁ and universally quantifying vertex palettes of cardinality at most ℵ₀. These restrictions are equivalent to the source's cardinal-sized colourings, including when the vertex type lies in a higher universe.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any countable palette, even in a higher universe, injects into ℕ. Composing a vertex colouring with that injection preserves its colour classes, and ℕ itself is among the permitted palettes. An edge palette of size ℵ₁ can be bijectively relabelled by a fixed universe-0 representative of ℵ₁; containing every edge colour is invariant under this relabelling. In /workspace/review/palettes.lean, complete_rhs_iff_fixed proves the entire RHS equivalent to using this fixed edge palette and ℕ vertex colours. A separate lemma verifies the extension to higher-universe countable vertex palettes. The equivalence proof does not depend on sorryAx.
